unite_adi: UPPER SECONDARY-PREP YEAR-LEVEL: B1 - THEME 15: LIFE IN NATURE AND GLOBAL PROBLEMS

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students will design and present a project that explores the challenges and solutions related to natural resources, wildlife, and environmental protection. They will research the importance of conserving natural resources and animal habitats, analyse the effects of human activity on nature, and propose actionable steps for a more sustainable future. As part of the project, students will write reports, create visual aids (such as posters or presentations), and role-play as conservationists, scientists, or environmental activists. They will simulate scenarios like addressing climate change, protecting endangered species, or raising awareness about sustainable practices. The assignment will be evaluated using rubrics. bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''life in nature and global problems with its components such as natural resources, animals in nature and their habitats, protecting natural resources and animals'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school may know what natural resources, animals in nature and their habitats, protecting natural resources and animals mean in their own language as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in another language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''life in nature and global problems'' in English from previous themes and/or years such as ''to go camping, walking, resource, habitat and so on'' and also some structures such as ''If they do not take necessary precautions, some species may become extinct. If he left earlier, he would not be stuck in traffic.'' in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''natural resources, animals in nature and their habitats, protecting natural resources and animals'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, small pictures could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss the pictures in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To help students reflect on environmental issues in English by using target grammar and target vocabulary in a meaningful context to describe past actions and suggest better solutions. Activity 1: Writing Reflection-Letter to the Future Generation Students write a letter to a future generation about past actions that harmed the environment and suggest better solutions, such as ''We had polluted rivers before realising the harm'', or ''If we had recycled earlier, we could have reduced waste''. The letters include at least three environmental issues and vocabulary like pollution, recycling, and habitat loss. After writing, students place their letters in a box. One student picks a letter randomly, reads it aloud, and shares their thoughts with the class. The teacher gives feedback at the end, focusing on target grammar and target vocabulary use. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To help students identify natural resources, animals, and habitats in English by using target vocabulary through a fun game. Activity 1: Bingo Nature Bingo is a fun vocabulary activity. Students use 5x5 bingo cards with pictures representing target vocabulary words (e.g., a recycling bin for recycling, a polar bear for endangered species). The teacher prepares word cards that match these pictures, draws them randomly like in tombola, and reads the word aloud. The teacher can also show the word to beginners. Students listen carefully, find the matching picture, and mark it on their bingo cards with markers or chips. The game ends when a student marks five pictures in a row (horizontally, vertically, or diagonally) and shouts ''Bingo!'' to win. Optionally, the first student to mark three pictures can call out ''Chinco!'' as a milestone. The teacher gives constructive and supportive feedback to students to encourage their learning. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
